title: Cocones on the constant point diagram and their colimit criterion
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences, coherent transformations and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal W$, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal W$-small spaces defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], formed in a containing universe. Let $K$ be a $\mathcal W$-small simplicial set, $Y$ a $\mathcal W$-small Kan complex, and $*=\Delta^0$ the one-point space. Write $\Delta_KZ$ for the constant diagram on $Z$. There is a natural equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(\Delta_K*,\Delta_KY)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,Y).$$
It identifies a coherent family of maps from the point to $Y$ with its family of points of $Y$, including all simplicial parameters. For a coherent cocone $\lambda:\Delta_K*\to\Delta_KY$, let $e_\lambda:K\to Y$ be the map corresponding to its point under this equivalence, up to homotopy. Then $\lambda$ is colimiting if and only if $e_\lambda$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No nonemptiness or connectedness condition is imposed on $K$ or $Y$.

source.place: Kerodon Example 7.1.2.10 (03F8), using the copower criterion in Proposition 7.1.2.8 (03F6) and the spaces mapping comparison in Example 4.6.7.7 (06QR). The displayed cocone-space formula is the exponential adjunction for constant diagrams composed with that comparison. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $C=\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ and $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)$. All auxiliary constructions involving the category of all small Kan complexes are performed in the containing universe, while $K,Y$ and the eventual test targets remain $\mathcal W$-small. The enriched morphism sets $\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z)$ are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan]; [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory] makes $C$ a quasicategory. The functor/cone calculus makes $D$ a quasicategory. We use the arrow mapping space $U_C(X,Z)$ and its specified equivalence $j:\operatorname{Map}_C(X,Z)\to U_C(X,Z)$ from [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The realization criterion [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] has two useful immediate consequences used below: weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three, since precomposition on each Kan-target homotopy-class set does; and simplicially homotopic maps, or maps joined by a zigzag of simplicial homotopies, are weak equivalences simultaneously, since they induce the same maps on these sets.

source.place: Preparatory hypotheses; Cordier--Porter, Kerodon 2.4.5.1 (00LJ), and right-pinch comparison 4.6.5.10 (01L5)

proof.text: Use $J^n,Q^n,|-|_Q,\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ and the natural weak equivalences $p_A:|A|_Q\to A$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. We need the explicit maximum map $q^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$, not an unstated choice of $p$. In the subset-poset model of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n+1}]$, send a subset $B$ in a morphism from an initial vertex to the last vertex to $\max(B\setminus\{n+1\})$. All morphisms within the initial face go to the identity of one object $x$; the last object is $y$, with morphism set $\Delta^n$ from $x$ to $y$, singleton endomorphisms and no reverse morphisms. Union with a subset in the initial face does not change this maximum, since its elements precede the source of the final segment. Thus the enriched map factors through $\mathfrak C[J^n]$, defining $q^n$. Inclusion of subsets makes the maximum monotone. For every monotone $a:[m]\to[n]$, $\max(a(B))=a(\max B)$, proving cosimplicial naturality. This yields $q_A:|A|_Q\to A$. To compare it with the $p$ supplied by the node, form the simplicial map $r^n=\max(p^n,q^n):Q^n\to\Delta^n$ pointwise in the ordered set $[n]$. The inequalities $p^n\leq r^n\geq q^n$ give simplicial homotopies natural in $n$: on a simplex, use the smaller value before the switch in $\Delta^1$ and the larger afterwards. They descend through the coend to $p_A\simeq r_A\simeq q_A$; products with $\Delta^1$ commute with the displayed coproducts and quotient relations degreewise. Step 1 now shows that every $q_A$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: HTT Section 2.2.2, explicit maximum map and coend; comparison with the stated existential p expanded here

proof.text: For Kan $X,Z$ put $T=\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z)$ and $M=\operatorname{Map}_C(X,Z)$. The coherent-nerve adjunction identifies $M$ exactly with $\operatorname{Sing}_QT$: a right-pinched simplex is an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$ with endpoints $X,Z$. The collapsed initial face forces its endomorphisms to be identities; the sole remaining datum is its map $Q^n\to T$. Define $\alpha:T\to M$ in degree $n$ by $t\mapsto t q^n$. This is natural in $n$. The evaluation counit $\epsilon_T:|\operatorname{Sing}_QT|_Q\to T$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], and $\epsilon_T|\alpha|_Q=q_T$, checked on each coend summand by evaluation. Hence $|\alpha|_Q$ is a weak equivalence. Naturality gives $p_M|\alpha|_Q=\alpha p_T$; two-out-of-three proves that $\alpha$ is a weak equivalence. Both $T$ and $M$ are Kan, by Steps 1 and the pinch comparison. For clarity this gives an actual simplicial homotopy inverse: the realization criterion tested at $T$ gives $g:M\to T$ with $[g\alpha]=[1_T]$; its injectivity tested at $M$ gives $[\alpha g]=[1_M]$. Here brackets mean edge-components of internal functor objects. These objects are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], so each finite zigzag of edges compresses to one edge: reverse an edge by filling an outer $2$-horn with an identity edge, then compose by filling an inner $2$-horn. Thus both class equalities are simplicial homotopies. Composing with $j$ gives a homotopy equivalence $b_{X,Z}=j\alpha:\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z)\to U_C(X,Z)$, taking each map to its corresponding edge.

source.place: HTT Section 2.2.2, evaluation counit; Kerodon 4.6.7.7 (06QR), with the right-pinched comparison proved from the existing resolution

proof.text: There is an actual degreewise isomorphism $U_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KZ)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,U_C(X,Z))$: on both sides an $n$-simplex is a map $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ whose endpoint restrictions are constant at $X$ and $Z$. Currying and interchanging the two parameter factors give inverse maps, commuting with every restriction map. Postcomposition with $b_{X,Z}$ is a homotopy equivalence on internal functor objects: postcompose with its homotopy inverse, and curry its two homotopies, evaluated at each point of $K$ with the same interval parameter. Together with $j_D$, this gives a natural zigzag of equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KZ)\to U_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KZ)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,U_C(X,Z))\leftarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))$. At $X=*$, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(*,Z)$ with $Z$, giving the required displayed equivalence. An edge cocone $\lambda$ is a vertex of the middle arrow space; the homotopy inverse supplies a map $e_\lambda:K\to Y$ whose image is homotopic to that vertex. It is determined up to homotopy. The constructions commute with restriction in $K$ and preserve all simplicial parameters; no isomorphism between the right-pinched space and the enriched morphism set is asserted.

source.place: Constant-diagram exponential calculation in the arrow model; right-pinch Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5)

proof.text: Check composition, which is needed for the particular cocone rather than merely an abstract equivalence of its space. For Kan $X,Y,Z$ and $n$-simplices $f:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$, $g:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Z)$, construct a simplex $\Phi(g,f)$ of $V_C(X,Y,Z)$ from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. For a chain of vertices in $[2]\times[n]$, send the three layers to $X,Y,Z$ and all within-layer morphisms to identities. On a subset $B$ joining layer $0$ to layer $1$, evaluate $f$ at the largest parameter among its layer-$0$ vertices; on a subset joining $1$ to $2$, evaluate $g$ at the largest parameter among its layer-$1$ vertices. On a subset joining $0$ to $2$, put $s=\max\{i:(0,i)\in B\}$ and $t=\max\{i:(a,i)\in B,\ a\leq1\}$ and assign $g(t)\circ f(s)$, as a map on the nerve of the subset poset. Both coordinates are monotone under inclusion. Splitting a subset at a layer-$1$ vertex gives precisely the union-composition formula; splitting within layer $0$ or $2$ only inserts an identity. Hence these formulas define enriched functors on every simplex, compatible on faces and degeneracies, and so a map $\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to C$. Its edges are $b(f),b(g),b(g\circ f)$: on the $02$ face there is no layer $1$, so $t=s$. Monotone parameter changes preserve these maxima, proving compatibility in all degrees. The characterization by $V,\theta,\ell$ in the cited composition node therefore identifies enriched composition with coherent composition up to homotopy: $\theta\Phi=b\times b$ and $\ell\Phi=b\circ(\text{composition})$ for this map $\Phi$, so $[j][c][\alpha\times\alpha]=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}[b\times b]=[\ell\Phi]=[j][\alpha][\text{composition}]$, and $j$ is a homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.6.8.19 (02LN), right-pinched version of the explicit three-layer construction

proof.text: Transfer the composition comparison of Step 5 to constant diagrams. Currying gives $V_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KY,\Delta_KZ)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,V_C(X,Y,Z))$, with the restriction maps $\theta,\ell$ given pointwise, so the same compatibility holds for constant diagrams. In particular the test map induced by $\lambda$ becomes $h\mapsto h\circ e_\lambda$ under Step 4, since $j$ is natural under the simplicial functor $\Delta_K:C\to D$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], so $\Delta_K$ on mapping spaces becomes the constant-map inclusion $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Z))$, and the edge $\lambda$ is a vertex of $\operatorname{Map}_D$ corresponding to $e_\lambda$, including every higher parameter; replacing $\lambda$ by its homotopic representative preserves this test map up to homotopy. This also supplies naturality of the comparison in the space variable and its coherent composition parameters.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.6.8.19 (02LN) applied pointwise in K; constant-diagram currying as in Kerodon Example 7.1.2.10 (03F8)

proof.text: By the dual cocone clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the specified cocone $\lambda:\Delta_K*\to\Delta_KY$ is colimiting if and only if, for every $\mathcal W$-small Kan complex $Z$, precomposition induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_C(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(\Delta_K*,\Delta_KZ)$. The comparison of Step 3 identifies the source with $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Z)$; Step 4 identifies the target with $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$; Steps 5 and 6 identify the actual arrow with $e_\lambda^*$. Thus the criterion is exactly that all $e_\lambda^*:\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$ be weak equivalences. This uses the specified apex $Y$ and assumes no prior existence of another colimit.

If $e_\lambda$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] applies with $A=K$, $B=Y$ and each test Kan complex $Z$. It makes $e_\lambda^*$ a simplicial homotopy equivalence. The passage to a weak equivalence is precisely [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], without a Kan or nonemptiness condition on $K$. Step 7 then makes $\lambda$ colimiting.

Conversely, a colimiting $\lambda$ gives weak equivalences $e_\lambda^*$ for all $\mathcal W$-small Kan $Z$ by Step 7. Their maps on edge-components are bijections: apply the forward implication of [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] to each of these weak equivalences, and use the two Kan targets equal to its source and its target to construct a homotopy inverse by the two-test argument of Step 3. A homotopy inverse induces inverse functions on edge-components. The converse criterion in [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence], now applied to $v=e_\lambda:K\to Y$ in $\mathcal W$, proves that $e_\lambda$ induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups. This is the required weak homotopy equivalence. When $K=\varnothing$ the test $Z=\varnothing$ forces $Y=\varnothing$; if $Y=\varnothing$ and a cocone exists then $e_\lambda$ forces $K=\varnothing$. For disconnected $K$ the criterion retains all components, and for a simplicial circle $K$ and $Y=*$ it fails on higher homotopy. Thus no nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis was used.

lean.statement: theorem space_point_cocone_criterion : ∃ b : ∀ (K : SSet.{u}) (Y : Kan.{u}), pointCoconeIndex ((ihom K).obj Y.obj) ⟶ pointCoconeArrowSpace K Y, ∀ (K : SSet.{u}) (Y : Kan.{u}), PointCoconeFamilyFormula K Y (b K Y) ∧ SSet.KanComplex (pointCoconeMappingSpace K Y) ∧ SSet.KanComplex (pointCoconeArrowSpace K Y) ∧ SSet.KanComplex (pointCoconeIndex ((ihom K).obj Y.obj)) ∧ (∃ r : pointCoconeArrowSpace K Y ⟶ pointCoconeIndex ((ihom K).obj Y.obj), Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (b K Y ≫ r) (𝟙 _)) ∧ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (r ≫ b K Y) (𝟙 _))) ∧ (∃ j : pointCoconeMappingSpace K Y ⟶ pointCoconeArrowSpace K Y, PointCoconePinchFormula K Y j ∧ ∃ r : pointCoconeArrowSpace K Y ⟶ pointCoconeMappingSpace K Y, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (j ≫ r) (𝟙 _)) ∧ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (r ≫ j) (𝟙 _))) ∧ (∀ t : SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory (pointCoconeDiagram K pointCoconePoint) _⦋0⦌, t.1.1 = pointCoconeVertex Y → (∃ e : K ⟶ Y.obj, PointCoconeRepresents K Y (b K Y) t e) ∧ (∀ e : K ⟶ Y.obj, PointCoconeRepresents K Y (b K Y) t e → (SSet.Enhanced.IsColimiting (pointCoconeDiagram K pointCoconePoint) t ↔ SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence e)))
lean.note: The natural equivalence is the canonical zigzag through fixed-endpoint arrow spaces, with actual simplicial homotopy inverses for both legs. The family-of-points leg is fixed on every enriched simplex by the maximum initial-vertex formula; the pinch leg is fixed by its prism formula. The criterion applies to every representative of the given cocone up to fixed-endpoint homotopy. All helper definitions and the constant-vertex structural proof obligation belong to this node; small and containing universes remain distinct.
